statement_summary: Roles designated in writing (system owner, security coordinator, product security lead, 524B owner)
Risk assessment each July, at design freeze, and before each submission
Risk acceptance authority; High risks never accepted
Sanctions recorded; good-faith reporting protected
Written security terms before vendors receive data; contract manufacturer terms with 72-hour incident notice
Annual independent evaluation and before each submission
Retention of security records (6 years or QMS period if longer)
Annual policy review; policies available in the eQMS
Written, risk-rated, time-limited exceptions; none for shared device credentials
Security requirements, threat model, SBOM, security testing, and release record for every release
Signing only through the release pipeline with an HSM-backed key and two approvers
No hardcoded, default, or shared device credentials; unique per-unit credentials
Named accounts only; sealed break-glass cloud owner account
Least privilege with written approval by the system owner
MFA on every account and administrator login, including MSP-held logins
Offboarding on the last day across all systems; contractor accounts with end dates
Monthly account reconciliation; quarterly privilege review
Secrets only in the CI secret store or key service; leaked secrets rotated in 5 business days
Named vendor, contractor, and test lab accounts with MFA; yearly MSP technician list
Lab workstations with named logins, MSP patching, and a separate network segment
Password length and no reuse
Company systems for company work; need-to-know access
No Restricted or Confidential data in personal accounts or unapproved AI tools
Lock screens; never share passwords, MFA codes, or signing approvals
Security training yearly; secure development training for engineers; phishing simulations
Report suspected incidents and vulnerabilities at once
Call-back check on bank detail changes
Signed policy acknowledgment
Product security incident runbook kept and printed
Report within 1 hour to the right incident lead
Log every incident and vulnerability report
Published CVD policy and contact; 3-business-day acknowledgment; agreed disclosure date
Exploitability and safety assessment; controlled or uncontrolled risk recorded
Regular security maintenance cycle and out-of-cycle fixes for critical vulnerabilities
Complaint, MDR, and correction decisions after marketing
Insurer hotline first for data theft or extortion; MSP engaged
Ransom only with approvals and an OFAC check
Supplier incident reports logged and handled
Annual tabletop with the MSP and before commercial distribution
Lessons learned within 30 days; threat model and risk register updated
Three classification levels (Restricted, Confidential, Public)
Encrypt Restricted and Confidential data at rest and in transit
Data kept only in approved systems; keys only in the key service or CI secret store
Asset inventory and an SBOM for each released software item
New vendors and tools approved with security terms before receiving data
SBOM Confidential until release; unfixed vulnerability details Restricted until disclosure
Approved AI tools only; no code, keys, or vulnerability details in public chatbots
Quarterly eQMS export; 30-day cloud snapshots; tested key recovery; restore tests twice a year
Wipe or certified destruction; returned units reflashed
Retention of design history, security records, and workforce data
No patient data in the cloud service before BAAs and a HIPAA program
regulatory_driver: Planned HIPAA obligation (45 CFR 164.308(b)) after clearance
